text.text_excerpt: I stayed in New Orleans for the week of Halloween, so I made sure to stop by all the cemeteries and voodoo shops possible (which I would've done even in July...I just find that kind of thing fascinating). I went to every voodoo shop in the Quarter, and this was definitely my favorite. What you read in reviews on here is true: they pretty successfully walk a fine line between touristy and legit. There's a very interesting and relatively extensive selection, and it was the only shop where I could find a few items I was satisfied with. There were a couple of young employees in there the first time I went in that were friendly, but the second day I went in, there was a man who was pretty rude...

Really liked this store- it's owned by the people who created Marie Laveau's voodoo shop and is almost a replica of the other store. They have tarot card readings in the back as well. Same items- candles, bags of charms, gris gris bags, wooden statues, saints, and all other types of luck items from around the world. I bought a potion here for $3 called "Confusion". Not sure if I want to rub it on anyone (may have helped kill a pet guinea pig with "healing potion" from a witchcraft store as a kid) but it was bright purple in the bottle and looked really cool. Tons of tarot cards to choose from- they are kind of pricey. You can probably order some online for cheaper but if you are like me t...

Reverend Zombie's House of Voodoo is a cool shop to stop into if you're exploring the French Quarter. They have tons of Voodoo items, dolls, masks, charms, books, spells, candles, and other awesome New Orleans novelty merchandise. In my opinion it's an awesome spot to pick up souvenirs if you're visiting the area, because then you're taking home something that isn't your typical kitschy souvenir, but rather an interesting and unique part of the city. They also perform readings in the shop. As someone who absolutely loves photos I was saddened by the fact that there are signs everywhere that say, "no photography."
